mechanism: tool_output_token_limit caps the tokens stored per tool output in history; over-limit output is truncated or summarised before storing. mcp_servers.<id>.tools.<tool>.output_token_limit overrides it per MCP tool (per-tool overrides added in v0.152.0 per a third-party blog).
default_limit: tool_output_token_limit: default not stated on official page; a mirrored example config and blogs say 10000 tokens (secondary source, unverified)
published_number: skills.max_context_tokens defaults to 2% of the model context window, explicit values capped at 10000; blog recommends 12000 for most workflows (unverified)
steal_for_claude_code: Per-tool-result token cap with a per-MCP-server override, so one noisy MCP tool cannot flood history; keep the cap configurable per tool.

mechanism: model_auto_compact_token_limit triggers history compaction at a token threshold; model_auto_compact_token_limit_scope chooses whether the threshold counts the full active context (total) or only growth after the carried compaction-window prefix (body_after_prefix). compact_prompt and experimental_compact_prompt_file override the compaction prompt.
default_limit: unset: model defaults apply; scope defaults to total
steal_for_claude_code: Expose the compaction trigger as a setting and let it count only growth after the carried prefix, so a long cached prefix does not force compaction early.

mechanism: Tool output truncation moves to token budgets with a TruncationPolicy per model family; legacy GPT-5.1 family uses a byte budget (Bytes(10_000)); truncated structured output is replaced with a marker '[omitted {n} text items ...]'. Reviewer flags that the summary marker can push stored output past the cap when budget is zero.
default_limit: TruncationPolicy::Bytes(10_000) for the legacy GPT-5.1 family (10 KiB)
steal_for_claude_code: Use an explicit omitted-count marker in truncated tool output so the model knows how much it did not see; count the marker against the cap.

mechanism: Shell and MCP outputs are written to a file instead of truncated; the agent runs tail to see the end and reads further only when needed. Full chat history is saved to a file, and after summarisation the agent searches it for details the summary dropped. MCP tool descriptions sync to one folder per server and only tool names stay in static context; terminal output is synced to files the agent greps.
published_number: A/B test: total agent tokens reduced 46.9% in runs that called an MCP tool (variance depends on how many MCP servers are installed); no absolute token counts or truncation thresholds published
steal_for_claude_code: Spill any tool output over a size to a file under the project scratch dir and return only a head line plus the path; keep full chat history on disk so post-compaction recovery can grep it; load MCP tool schemas on demand.

mechanism: Handoff replaces compaction: the user states a goal for a new thread; Amp analyses the current thread and drafts a starter prompt plus a list of relevant files; the draft is editable before sending. It extracts what matters for the next task instead of summarising the whole thread, since stacked summaries are lossy.
steal_for_claude_code: Goal-directed handoff for seat-fresh: the new chat starts from a generated prompt plus a relevant-file list, not a rolling summary; the goal line is the input.

mechanism: Subagent described as a mini-Amp the main agent spawns for a specific task; it runs in its own context window and the main conversation sees only the final result. Oracle runs in an isolated context window (secondary source; Amp manual not retrieved).
steal_for_claude_code: Isolate research and exploration in sub-agents that return only a final answer, so intermediate tool calls never enter the parent context (matches the scout/librarian pattern in the harness).

mechanism: Repo map: a concise map of key classes and functions with types and call signatures, built from tree-sitter tags and ranked by a graph algorithm over files with dependencies; the most referenced identifiers are kept until the budget is full.
default_limit: --map-tokens default 1k tokens; map can expand beyond it when no files are added to the chat
published_number: 1k tokens default; no benchmarks or share-of-context figures published
steal_for_claude_code: Give Claude Code a fixed-budget ranked symbol map of the repo (names and signatures, most-referenced first) at session start, so orientation costs about 1k tokens instead of file reads.

mechanism: Tree-sitter parses source into an AST to find definitions and references; the map shows each file's key symbols and the critical lines of their definitions. tags.scm queries adapted from several open tree-sitter grammars.
steal_for_claude_code: If building a map, parse definitions with tree-sitter and rank by reference counts; no need for an LLM to scan files for orientation.

mechanism: Auto compaction triggers when a session nears the model limit, leaving a buffer. Everything except the most recent conversation is summarised into a structured summary (objective, decisions, active work, blockers, relevant files) placed before the recent turns; later compactions update the same summary. Long tool output in the kept recent turns is shortened; if a provider rejects the request as too long, it compacts and retries once.
default_limit: keep.tokens default 15000 (recent turns kept verbatim); buffer default 10% of the model limit
published_number: Example config uses keep.tokens 24000 and buffer 16000; no tool-output cap published
steal_for_claude_code: Keep the last ~15k tokens verbatim and summarise the rest into a fixed structured schema; retry once on a too-long rejection instead of failing the turn.

mechanism: Deduplication strategy finds repeated tool calls (such as reading the same file repeatedly) and keeps only the most recent output; obsolete outputs are replaced by a placeholder before each request, which is non-destructive. An optional AI analysis strategy judges relevance at LLM cost.
published_number: One fork's testing: cache hit rate about 65% with DCP vs about 85% without (unverified fork report)
steal_for_claude_code: Dedupe repeated reads of the same file in the request view (keep latest, placeholder the older copies), but weigh it against prompt-cache hit loss since pruning changes the prefix.

mechanism: Older tool-call outputs are summarised in the background while recent calls stay in full detail; cutoff is computed from the model context limit and compaction threshold. Auto-compaction starts at a fraction of the context limit, with a separate token cap; setting threshold to 0 disables it.
default_limit: Tool-output summarisation starts after more than 10 tool calls in a session (GOOSE_TOOL_CALL_CUTOFF); auto-compact at 80% of limit or 225000 tokens, whichever is first; default global context limit 128000
published_number: CLI context indicator: green under 50%, yellow 50-85%, red above 85%
steal_for_claude_code: Background-summarise tool results older than the last N calls (N about 10) and keep recent ones verbatim; a token cap below the provider long-context tier (for example 225k) keeps long-context pricing from triggering.

mechanism: Auto Compact tracks token use as the chat nears the model limit and replaces history with a summary that keeps technical details, code changes and decisions; file changes stay intact. Models without it fall back to rule-based truncation. Checkpoints can restore earlier states.
steal_for_claude_code: Checkpoint before compaction so a bad summary can be rolled back; fall back to deterministic truncation when the summary step fails.
